title: Expand a commercial-cleaning business with evidence from the route
description: Test supervision, account quality, customer payment and delivery economics before offering U.S. rights.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the account and the route
paragraphs: For an established cleaning company, the useful unit is often an account cluster served by a team and supervisor, not a retail outlet. Compare customer type, usable service hours, site access, travel, recurring frequency and contract length. A home-market annual contract is evidence of delivery there; it does not establish U.S. demand, labour availability or procurement acceptance.

sections.heading: Model the costs that a branch manager does not remove
paragraphs: Assign responsibility for estimating labour, winning bids, replacing absent staff, responding to complaints and managing receivables. Price dedicated management and quality supervision before a royalty. Then test account concentration: losing one large building can leave paid supervisory time, vehicles and route gaps while the revenue disappears.

sections.heading: Separate law, customer conditions and practice
paragraphs: OSHA identifies cleaning-industry chemical, equipment and workplace hazards and links applicable general-industry standards. Build the actual task/product safety review with the responsible employer. A customer’s insurance certificate, background-screening or service-level requirement is a procurement condition unless separately required by law; record its source and cost.

sections.heading: Use an original fictional pilot
paragraphs: Fictional example: investigate three nearby office buildings rather than assume a national rollout. Record bid process, required service times, equipment storage, staffing cover, client sign-off and collection terms for each. Unknown travel time or wage evidence remains missing; it does not improve a market score.

sections.heading: Prepare before the next bid
paragraphs: Output: an account-level pilot brief owned by the COO with the finance lead.
bullets: Record client type, tender date, contract renewal and termination provisions.
Map service hours, travel, supervision and emergency cover.
Obtain insurance and customer-procurement requirements separately from law.
Track invoice acceptance, disputes and actual receipt dates.
Define who receives and serves national accounts.
Test a paid, lawfully arranged pilot without implying that it authorises franchise offers.

limitations: No location-specific wage, tax, customer demand or safety clearance.

title: Separate the facilities contract from the work that needs a license
description: Map each service, employer and subcontractor before transferring a facilities-management model.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: One customer contract can contain many regulated activities
paragraphs: Facilities services can include cleaning, planned maintenance, access systems, pest control, landscaping and repairs. Describe the exact tasks rather than presume that a facilities brand license permits every activity. Map what the partner performs, subcontracts and merely coordinates. Local professional, contractor and sector requirements can change that allocation.

sections.heading: Build the service-level responsibility map
paragraphs: A service-level agreement describes contracted performance: response time, completion evidence, exclusions, escalation and credits. Assign who dispatches, approves additional work, invoices, handles emergencies and bears rework. Customer procurement may demand specific insurance, references or approved subcontractors. Those contractual requirements deserve a separate category from government rules.

sections.heading: Investigate actual permit and licence triggers
paragraphs: The SBA directs businesses to licenses according to activity and location. Start with the named state, municipality, county and worksite; record the authority for each trade or operating question. A subcontractor’s own licence does not resolve every duty of the principal contracting or employing entity.

sections.heading: Fictional operating example
paragraphs: A fictional partner wins one multi-site customer with 60-day invoice terms. The partner must pay technicians and subcontractors earlier, while the customer can dispute incomplete service evidence. The relevant test is both gross margin and dated cash collection. Model the national customer’s failure separately from a broad market-sales percentage.

sections.heading: Reusable preparation checklist
paragraphs: Output: a service-by-service operating and procurement matrix.
bullets: Break the offer into tasks, locations and contracting parties.
Record accountable employer and competent operating lead.
Identify public authorisation, customer condition and insurer condition separately.
Price emergency response, subcontractor management and service credits.
Trace national-account allocation and cross-territory work.
Collect evidence before promising the full service bundle.

practicalOutput: Facilities task, licence and customer-condition matrix

title: A pest-control brand needs an operating certification plan
description: Check people, products and operating jurisdictions before estimating a U.S. pest-control launch.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Begin with the application work
paragraphs: A pest-control partner needs more than the right to use a name. List target pests, treatment method, sites, products and the people applying or supervising them. Distinguish product authorisation from applicator certification and any business licence. Home-country training can be useful evidence of capability but does not itself establish U.S. authorisation.

sections.heading: The federal starting point and local extension
paragraphs: EPA explains that restricted-use pesticide applicators or supervisors need certification under relevant rules and that state, territorial and tribal authorities administer certification. Many states have broader requirements for commercial work. Investigate each operating jurisdiction and category before assigning a technician or assuming cross-state portability.

sections.heading: Make route economics match service obligations
paragraphs: Recurring service contracts can create route density, but callbacks, emergency jobs, seasonal demand, storage and customer access affect capacity. A large territory with scattered accounts may consume the supervisor’s time. Record insurance requested by customers and actual spill, vehicle and product-use responsibilities; do not treat an insurance quote as regulatory approval.

sections.heading: Fictional decision
paragraphs: A fictional European brand proposes importing a familiar treatment product and starting in two neighbouring states. Split the launch into two workstreams: lawful product/import review and each state’s people/business authorisations. A U.S.-sourced product may change inventory logistics but does not erase applicator obligations.

sections.heading: Reusable launch checklist
paragraphs: Output: a product/person/jurisdiction map.
bullets: Identify actual products and label-directed sites/uses.
Name the certifying authority for each area and category.
Record who is qualified and what supervision is required.
Assign storage, transport, customer notice and incident questions.
Obtain route, seasonality and callback evidence.
Keep unsupported certification, fee and insurance inputs unresolved.

limitations: No state certification or specific product conclusion.

title: Validate industrial-maintenance delivery before selling territory
description: Price competent supervision, downtime commitments and site safety against a narrow first service cluster.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Define the work more narrowly than the brand
paragraphs: Industrial maintenance may range from inspection to machine servicing, electrical work and process-critical repair. Document the equipment, task boundaries, customer qualification process and escalation rights. Professional or trade licensing, site-access rules and customer engineering approval can determine what the partner may actually deliver.

sections.heading: Hazardous energy is an operating workstream
paragraphs: OSHA’s general-industry overview explains hazardous-energy risks in servicing and maintenance and points to 29 CFR 1910.147. For covered work, the responsible employer needs appropriate energy-control procedures and training. Identify actual tasks and host-contractor interfaces; this guide does not decide exemptions or replace the customer-site procedure.

sections.heading: Test the economics of a response promise
paragraphs: A four-hour response promise is a staffing, geography and spare-parts decision. Model on-call pay, specialist cover, travel, calibration, tools, insurance and subcontractors. Separate a customer’s production loss exposure from the service fee. Record liability and service-credit negotiation as a contract workstream with financial review.

sections.heading: Fictional first-market test
paragraphs: A fictional Dutch brand chooses one industrial corridor for customer interviews and a permitted pilot. The team asks what suppliers must demonstrate before a bid, how shutdown windows are scheduled and who approves a new technician. A national population total is not evidence that those procurement gates can be passed.

sections.heading: Reusable evidence checklist
paragraphs: Output: a first-corridor delivery and qualification brief.
bullets: List specific assets and tasks within scope.
Document competencies, local trade questions and supervision.
Map each customer’s procurement, safety and insurance requirements.
Model response time using real dispatch and travel assumptions.
Separate recurring maintenance revenue from one-off shutdown projects.
Fund support and specialist escalation without relying on territory-sale fees.

practicalOutput: Industrial-service scope, safety and response-capacity brief
limitations: Task-specific OSHA, state-plan and trade scope remains to be reviewed.

title: Test whether technical decisions can travel without the founder
description: Document authority, competence and escalation for a U.S. technical-services partner.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Find the decisions still owned by the founder
paragraphs: A technical-services company can have branch managers while the owner still approves every unusual job, specification, supplier substitution or warranty dispute. List those decisions and record frequency, response time and consequences. The goal is an operating responsibility map, not a questionnaire score proving that knowledge is transferable.

sections.heading: Distinguish experience from authorisation
paragraphs: Prepare a task list identifying whether each activity is inspection, advice, design, installation, repair or certification. The actual state, profession and worksite determine operating requirements. SBA’s location/activity approach is a starting point; neither a brand licence nor foreign professional status settles U.S. authority.

sections.heading: Price the escalation channel
paragraphs: Record support time for quotations, complex faults, documentation, audits and client meetings. If the U.S. manager must wait overnight for the European founder, a response promise can fail even with capable field staff. Cost a backup decision maker and define which decisions stay with the brand, partner and appropriately authorised professional.

sections.heading: Fictional validation task
paragraphs: For a fictional German testing-services brand, choose ten historic exception jobs. Ask a proposed manager to produce a decision and escalation record using sanitised facts. Compare decisions with the responsible technical lead. This exercise tests documentation gaps; it does not confer professional competence or guarantee future outcomes.

sections.heading: Reusable preparation checklist
paragraphs: Output: a competence-and-decision matrix.
bullets: Map owner-only technical, pricing and customer decisions.
Name the accountable decision maker and qualified backup.
Record evidence of training, observed performance and limits.
Separate customer accreditation from government authorisation.
Price remote and in-person escalation.
Define a bounded U.S. pilot before broad rights are granted.

practicalOutput: Technical decision authority and owner-dependence map
limitations: No professional credential or regulatory approval is issued.

title: Allocate access, support and incident duties in an IT-services model
description: Check who controls customer data and service continuity before a U.S. partner receives systems access.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the service and access map
paragraphs: IT support, managed services, software implementation and training have different access needs. Record who contracts with the customer, whose staff access systems, where access occurs, what data is involved and who authorises changes. Separate the brand’s software rights from a customer’s licence and security permissions.

sections.heading: Build a usable responsibility schedule
paragraphs: NIST provides small-business guidance on cybersecurity risks, incident response, cloud security and other topics. Use it as a preparation reference. It is not a universal law, an endorsement or a certification of your service. Actual customer, public-contract, sector and privacy requirements need their own evidence and scope.

sections.heading: Price the support window
paragraphs: A U.S. customer may expect service while the parent’s team sleeps. Cost on-call cover, escalation, third-party licences, secure onboarding/offboarding, backups, incident exercises and client reporting. Clarify who funds emergency work and who can communicate externally after an incident. Do not promise “24/7 support” without staffing and supplier commitments.

sections.heading: Fictional pilot
paragraphs: A fictional Southeast Asian managed-service brand gives one U.S. partner a limited customer support role. Before live access, the team rehearses a departed technician’s account removal and a suspicious-login report using a test environment. Record completion as an exercise, not proof of legal compliance or absence of security risk.

sections.heading: Reusable preparation checklist
paragraphs: Output: an access-and-incident responsibility schedule.
bullets: Record customer, provider and partner entities and actual data paths.
Define minimum necessary access and named approvers.
Map breach/incident escalation and contractual deadlines without inventing a universal deadline.
Record cross-border privacy questions and sector restrictions as unresolved until reviewed.
Budget licence, security and coverage costs per customer.
Test service continuity if the parent or partner is unavailable.

practicalOutput: IT data-access and incident responsibility schedule
limitations: No comprehensive federal/state or cross-border privacy assessment.

title: Distinguish business training from regulated credentials
description: Prepare a U.S. training model around delivery rights, instructor capability and claims that can be supported.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Describe the actual learning service
paragraphs: Business training may mean corporate workshops, technical instruction, employee assessment or a course marketed as qualifying someone for an occupation. State exactly what learners receive. A certificate of attendance, private brand certification, licence to practise and recognised professional credential are different things.

sections.heading: Investigate the relevant activity and location
paragraphs: SBA’s general licensing guidance ties requirements to the activity and operating location. Record where teaching, recruitment, assessment and customer contracting occur. If training touches a regulated occupation, childcare, healthcare or postsecondary education, move the relevant operating review ahead of sales promises. Do not imply that licensing a syllabus is enough.

sections.heading: Make the content and delivery rights usable
paragraphs: Record ownership and permitted use of slides, software, recordings, marks, learner materials and translations. Name who updates technical content and who can approve instructors. A well-run home-market branch may rely on the founder’s teaching or sales reputation; test whether another instructor can deliver the defined outcome.

sections.heading: Fictional economics exercise
paragraphs: A fictional European B 2 B training brand tests one paid corporate workshop through a properly reviewed arrangement. Record customer procurement, instructor preparation, venue/platform costs, travel, materials, cancellation terms and collection date. Do not multiply a full classroom’s gross revenue by every working day and call the result likely profit.

sections.heading: Reusable preparation checklist
paragraphs: Output: a course-rights and delivery-capability factsheet.
bullets: Describe the credential or attendance evidence precisely.
Identify sector or education authorisation questions before promotion.
Record intellectual-property rights and revision ownership.
Observe instructor delivery and assessment using stated criteria.
Price realistic utilisation, preparation and customer acquisition.
Keep customer outcome claims tied to actual evidence.

practicalOutput: Training rights, claims and delivery-capability factsheet
limitations: No professional or education authorisation determination.

title: Can the business deliver without the owner every day?
description: Map real decisions and evidence before treating branch managers as proof that the model transfers.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: A manager title is a starting fact
paragraphs: Management independence is the ability to make and deliver the important decisions when the owner is absent. Investigate sales, pricing, technical exceptions, key accounts, supplier negotiations, recruitment, quality and cash authorisations. A business can perform daily operations while still relying on the owner for the exceptions that protect margin and customers.

sections.heading: Use a responsibility map with evidence
paragraphs: For each responsibility, record accountable role, day-to-day decision maker, backup, authority limit and the most recent observed example. Distinguish a manual being written from a manager successfully using it. Record unresolved gaps instead of converting answers into a transferability score.

sections.heading: Fictional preparation exercise
paragraphs: In a fictional facilities company, the COO covers service delivery but the owner closes every contract above a chosen internal limit. The U.S. plan needs a local sales authority, realistic procurement time and parent support. The management payroll and support budget must include the people who would replace that work; the SBA finance guide supports the cost/cash discipline, not a required manager salary.

sections.heading: Test a bounded absence
paragraphs: Choose an internal, reversible exercise such as a planned week with documented escalation rules. Select ordinary and exception tasks in advance. Record what happened, who decided, delays, rework and customer effect. This is recommended business practice, not proof that U.S. delivery or legal obligations are satisfied.

sections.heading: Prepare the next decision
paragraphs: Output: an owner-dependence map before selecting a partner model.
bullets: List recurring decisions and consequential exceptions.
Name the role and backup with actual authority.
Record evidence date, limits and unresolved dependencies.
Cost replacement management and parent support separately.
Re-test after a change in offer, staffing or customer mix.
Choose further documentation, a smaller pilot, added capability or a pause.

practicalOutput: Responsibility map with owner dependencies and evidence dates
limitations: Business preparation only; no statutory readiness threshold.

title: Area developer or master operator: who will do the extra work?
description: Compare contracting, payments, recruitment and ongoing support before setting U.S. network rights.
reviewStatus: Merged into canonical guide after near-duplicate editorial review

sections.heading: Decide functions before labels
paragraphs: An own-unit operator delivers services in its own business. An area developer undertakes to open its own units over time. A master arrangement can authorise the recruitment and support of subfranchisees. An area representative may assist recruitment or support while the brand remains the contracting franchisor. Distribution and IP licensing need their own goods, payments and control facts.

sections.heading: Map three kinds of flow
paragraphs: Draw contracts, money and operating support separately. Who grants rights to the unit operator? Who collects initial and continuing payments? Who provides initial training, approves operators, supports bids, monitors quality and handles disputes? The definition in 16 CFR 436.1(k) includes subfranchisors performing pre-sale and post-sale functions; allocation in a contract does not erase regulatory duties.

sections.heading: Compare capability and funding
paragraphs: A partner may run excellent branches while lacking the staff and systems to recruit independent owners. List the extra roles and cost them before offering broad rights. Model the recurring support office using the revenue it can actually retain after the brand split, tax assumptions and obligations; treat unknown withholding as unresolved.

sections.heading: Fictional decision
paragraphs: A fictional brand expects the first partner to operate two branches, then recruit others. Phase 1 own-unit evidence should not automatically satisfy Phase 2 recruitment and support readiness. Write a separate decision gate with ownership, funding, sales-law review and support-capability evidence.

sections.heading: Preparation checklist
paragraphs: Output: a responsibility and payment diagram.
bullets: Identify every contracting and fee-receiving entity.
Separate own units from independent operator recruitment.
Assign pre-sale records and post-sale support.
Budget field visits, training, systems and local compliance work.
Test a delayed network and no new upfront fees.
Record unresolved federal and state definitions, disclosure and exemption questions.

limitations: No label-based franchise classification or allocation of legal liability.

title: What evidence would justify the first B 2 B market?
description: Use procurement and delivery evidence to narrow a market before committing a territory.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Match the customer buying process
paragraphs: Define the customer type, specific service, expected contract, procurement gate and service radius. Commercial regions are comparison tools, not legal jurisdictions. A large metro population does not establish demand for a specialised maintenance team or acceptance of a foreign brand.

sections.heading: Separate three evidence levels
paragraphs: An interview records a stated need. A tender invitation records a procurement opportunity. A signed customer contract records obligations, subject to its actual terms; it still does not establish profitable delivery or payment. Record the date, source, limitations and what observation would change the next decision.

sections.heading: Use a transparent comparison
paragraphs: Choose criteria before seeing scores: customer fit, sales cycle, staffing, route density, support access, operating requirements and cash terms. Let the team set weights. Keep unknown inputs visible and exclude a total ranking when a critical criterion lacks evidence; missing permit cost or insurance cannot become a favourable zero.

sections.heading: Fictional test
paragraphs: A fictional pest-control brand compares one dense office cluster with a larger dispersed territory. It interviews buyers, checks actual service categories and obtains local staffing and insurance evidence. The dense cluster can be easier to test, but that is a hypothesis pending evidence rather than a published “best market” claim.

sections.heading: Preparation checklist
paragraphs: Output: a market shortlist with the smallest useful validation activity.
bullets: State the customer segment and proposed operating boundary.
Record demand evidence separately from home-market assumptions.
Identify actual city, county, state and address-dependent tasks.
Quote costs with source, date, unit and scope.
Name the person, budget and date for the next validation.
Review law before offers, employment, imports or opening commitments.

practicalOutput: Market comparison with unknowns and a validation task
limitations: No ranking, search-demand statistics or unsourced cost averages.

title: A profitable service contract can still consume cash
description: Map invoicing, acceptance and collection before deciding how much working capital a U.S. unit needs.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Profit and cash answer different questions
paragraphs: For an accrual-based operating model, service revenue may be recorded before receipt. Payroll, materials and subcontractors can require earlier payment. SBA explains cash versus accrual accounting; the project needs a dated cash schedule alongside its operating-profit model.

sections.heading: Work back from the customer payment trigger
paragraphs: Read the proposed contract: when can an invoice be submitted, what evidence must accompany it, who approves it, when does the payment clock start and what disputes can defer payment? A nominal 30-day term may start after acceptance rather than after the technician attends. Model the actual process instead of inserting a universal receivables ratio.

sections.heading: Fictional cash bridge
paragraphs: Fictional example: the first month’s service generates $80,000 in invoices but no cash yet. Payroll and other payments due that month total $65,000. The operating budget alone cannot tell whether capital covers those dates. Add deposits, tax payments, equipment, financing receipts and later collections to a dated flow; do not count the same payroll again in a generic reserve.

sections.heading: Stress concentration and delay
paragraphs: Run downside, base and upside assumptions explicitly. Change customer start date, collection delay, dispute rate and staffing commitments as separate drivers. A large national account can improve density while increasing exposure to a single approval chain. A supplier credit term is financing only if it is actually available on stated conditions.

sections.heading: Preparation checklist
paragraphs: Output: a dated receivables and funding schedule.
bullets: Record service, invoice, acceptance and expected receipt dates.
Link labour and supplier payments to actual due dates.
Separate refundable deposits, expenditure and retained liquidity.
Mark uncommitted financing and unknown taxes as unresolved.
Derive peak funding from cumulative cash flows.
Assign the next evidence update to the finance lead.

practicalOutput: Dated cash-flow schedule and peak funding need
limitations: Illustrative amounts are fictional; no customer collection forecast.

title: Who owns the national account when local partners deliver?
description: Allocate selling, contracting, service, payment and credit before promising territorial rights.
reviewStatus: Merged into canonical guide after near-duplicate editorial review

sections.heading: A customer can buy nationally and receive service locally
paragraphs: A facilities or technical-services customer may negotiate centrally while operations occur in several partner territories. Separate lead ownership, contracting authority, service obligation, invoice recipient and margin allocation. “Exclusive territory” alone does not answer those questions.

sections.heading: Write an account-allocation schedule
paragraphs: Define reserved existing accounts, newly won national accounts, local branches of national buyers, online enquiries and jobs straddling boundaries. Include response, referral and dispute processes. The schedule should explain who approves pricing and how local delivery costs are considered. In a franchise, territory disclosures and terms need to align; the FTC guide’s Item 12 discussion is a reference point.

sections.heading: Fictional overlap
paragraphs: A fictional Dutch maintenance partner wins a customer whose headquarters is inside its area but whose first job is elsewhere. Another partner has local capacity. Compare a referral fee, local-service payment and central contract arrangement as commercial options; none is assumed lawful or enforceable without relevant review.

sections.heading: Protect service continuity and investment
paragraphs: Budget sales effort, equipment and training fairly. Define what happens if one operator cannot meet a national service obligation or an account changes scope. Avoid promising protection from independent competitors or suggesting that a contractual reservation overrides non-waivable local relationship rules.

sections.heading: Preparation checklist
paragraphs: Output: an account-allocation matrix before territory negotiation.
bullets: Classify accounts by actual contracting and service location.
Separate customer acquisition, fulfilment and collection.
Record channel, referral and pricing responsibilities.
Document expense and revenue allocation with an example.
Identify dispute, cure and continuity questions for review.
Make the disclosure and agreement consistent with the intended process.

limitations: No competition-law or territory-term enforceability opinion.

title: Build a partner evidence file without pretending to certify a person
description: Separate capability, available capital, records and unresolved questions before granting U.S. rights.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Evidence should answer a particular decision
paragraphs: The objective is to know what the candidate can fund and perform, what commitments it is taking and what still requires investigation. Use entity identity, authority, operating history, management capacity, accessible project capital, references and delivery evidence. Self-reported answers remain self-reported until the responsible person records what was checked and when.

sections.heading: Set lawful and proportionate scope
paragraphs: Do not collect passports, personal court files, bank statements or confidential customer contracts through this educational site. Describe the evidence and its custodian. If sensitive diligence is justified, use the appropriately authorised professional and secure process outside this tool. Record consent and access scope where applicable.

sections.heading: Court coverage is not one checkbox
paragraphs: PACER’s Case Locator is a national federal court index, including district, appellate and bankruptcy cases. State and local courts, administrative proceedings, arbitration and foreign records require separate scope decisions. An empty search is not proof that there are no disputes, nor does an allegation establish misconduct.

sections.heading: Fictional evidence decision
paragraphs: A fictional British facilities candidate reports ample wealth but leaves project allocation and supervisor availability unclear. Record separate tasks: dated capital-allocation confirmation, references for comparable delivery, and the named manager’s competing commitments. Do not improve a score because one field is blank.

sections.heading: Preparation checklist
paragraphs: Output: an evidence register with custodian, date, limit and next action.
bullets: Confirm entity name, identifiers and signing authority.
Separate net worth, liquidity, conditions and project allocation.
Observe relevant management and operating capability.
Document reference scope and contradictory evidence.
Record court systems, names searched, date and procedural outcomes.
Decide whether to investigate further, revise scope, run a pilot or pause.

limitations: No character, solvency, funding or compliance certification.

title: Compare FDD evidence against the model your team will actually operate
description: Use entity, year, management duties and cohort limits to avoid a misleading comparison.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Compare documents before comparing numbers
paragraphs: A Franchise Disclosure Document describes a particular seller and offering as of a particular issue or amendment date. Record entity, brand, year, state addenda, source URL and transaction scope. Do not mix one brand’s current fee table with another year’s financial results or assume a domestic owner-operated cohort matches a foreign brand’s management-run model.

sections.heading: Read management obligations alongside support
paragraphs: Item 15 concerns participation in actual operation; Item 11 describes assistance and training; Item 12 addresses territory. A manager-run assumption needs evidence from the actual offer and agreement. A reviewer should check all 23 items, not only the selected comparison fields. The FTC guide explains these disclosure subjects; it is not an endorsement of an offering.

sections.heading: Use the comparison as an evidence workspace
paragraphs: Capture Items 5–8 costs and sourcing;11–12 support and territory;15 participation;17 renewal, termination, transfer and disputes;19 any financial performance representation;20 outlet cohort and contacts;21 seller financial statements. Missing information remains missing, and automated extraction requires checking against the document.

sections.heading: Fictional cohort problem
paragraphs: A fictional service brand shows revenue from established units, while the team plans a new territory with a dedicated manager. Record cohort age, excluded units, service mix, owner effort and costs absent from revenue. Do not convert the number into a profit estimate or into a prospect-facing representation.

sections.heading: Preparation checklist
paragraphs: Output: a sourced, versioned FDD comparison worksheet.
bullets: Link the actual source and retain issue/amendment dates.
Record what each cited item says, not a guessed blank.
Check owner/manager participation in the offered model.
Record cohort definition, exclusions and limitations.
Keep financial statements separate from unit performance.
Assign unresolved interpretation and legal questions before commitment.

limitations: No FDD document extraction is published or deemed verified automatically.

title: Will a federal service contract change your labour cost model?
description: Identify covered wage and fringe obligations before reusing private-customer bid economics.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Check contract coverage first
paragraphs: The Department of Labor’s Service Contract Act guidance addresses covered federal and District of Columbia service contracts performed through service employees, subject to exceptions. For covered contracts over $2,500, applicable wage determinations and fringe benefits matter. A private customer’s tender is not automatically a federal service contract.

sections.heading: The budget needs the actual solicitation
paragraphs: Obtain the solicitation, incorporated clauses, wage determination, job descriptions, place of performance and any predecessor collective bargaining facts. Map actual duties to the relevant classifications. Do not price from a generic national minimum wage or assume a foreign company’s existing hourly rate is relevant.

sections.heading: Separate obligations from bid conditions
paragraphs: An agency or prime contractor may also require insurance, registration, financial capacity, references, security controls and reporting. Record each as a contract/procurement condition or a sourced legal requirement. The label matters because evidence, remedy and responsible role can differ.

sections.heading: Fictional bid review
paragraphs: A fictional cleaning partner expects one supervisor to cover several sites and uses its private-office bid template. The revised schedule must test the actual contract’s labour categories, benefits, staffing periods, travel and reporting. No wage amount is supplied here; without the relevant determination, the bid remains incomplete.

sections.heading: Preparation checklist
paragraphs: Output: a solicitation-to-cost checklist owned by the bid and payroll leads.
bullets: Record buyer, contract type and place of performance.
Identify applicable coverage, exceptions and clauses.
Obtain current wage determination and relevant predecessor facts.
Map worker duties and price wages, benefits and reporting.
Test payment timing and start-up funding.
Do not commit a bid while critical wage or staffing inputs remain unknown.

limitations: No specific solicitation, wage determination or exemption decision.
